    AI Overview
    Over 3.1 million bottles of eye drops, manufactured by
    K.C. Pharmaceuticals, have been recalled in April 2026 due to potential lack of sterility    . These products, which include various artificial tears and lubricants sold under store brands like CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, and Kroger, pose a risk of infection. 
    Key Information regarding the 2026 Recall: 
    • Manufacturer: K.C. Pharmaceuticals.
    • Reason: Lack of assurance of sterility, which may lead to infection.
    • Affected Products: Numerous eye drop types, including Dry Eye Relief, Artificial Tears Sterile Lubricant, Sterile Eye Drops Original Formula, and Redness Lubricant.
    • Retailers: CVS Health, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Kroger, Publix, H-E-B, Harris Teeter, Target, Dollar General, and more.
    • Action: Consumers should check their eye drops against the FDA list of recalled products and return them for a refund or discard them. 
    Affected Brand Examples (sold at): 
    • Walgreens: UPC: 3-11917-20167-2.
    • CVS Health: Multi-Action Relief, Lubricant Gel, and Lubricant Eye Drops.
    • Leader & TopCare: Various Sterile Eye Drops.
    • H-E-B: A.C. Eye Drops, Lubricant Eye Drops, and Original Eye Drops.
    • Foster & Thrive: NDC: 70677-1160-1. 
    The FDA has classified this as a Class II recall, suggesting that while the risk is low, there is a potential for temporary or reversible adverse health consequences.
